answers.stem_only: Receiving a message does not delete it. The message is hidden for the visibility timeout; when the timeout ends without a DeleteMessage call it becomes visible again and is received and processed again, repeatedly, until the retention period ends (no DLQ by default).
Use one SQS FIFO queue (exactly-once processing, ordering) and set the message group ID to the customer ID, so order holds per customer while different groups are consumed in parallel.

Amazon EventBridge: an event bus receives AWS service events, custom application events and SaaS partner events; one rule per service with an event pattern on detail fields routes events with no routing code.

For a standard queue, a message keeps its original enqueue timestamp when it moves to the dead-letter queue, so the DLQ retention period must cover 10 days from first send: raise the DLQ retention (to the 14-day maximum); the source queue can stay as is because messages leave it within an hour.
Create an EventBridge archive on the custom bus with 30-day retention, and use EventBridge replay for the affected time window after a fix.

Give the partner's HTTPS subscription a redrive policy (subscription-level dead-letter queue): an SQS queue in the same account and Region as the subscription, with a queue policy that lets SNS send; later redrive or resend the stored events.
Create an EventBridge Scheduler one-time (at) schedule per user that invokes the existing function 3 days later; SQS delays are limited to 15 minutes, so a queue delay cannot do it.

Put one SQS queue between the API and the single order service to buffer orders; the queue retains messages (days) while the service is offline and lets it consume at its own pace. No fan-out is needed for one consumer.
Amazon SNS topic with one subscription per microservice (pub/sub fan-out); the publisher does not know subscribers.
Amazon SNS: one topic, subscription filter policies per service, and SNS also delivers SMS to many phone numbers natively; EventBridge cannot send SMS without an extra SNS hop.

The default visibility timeout (30 seconds) is shorter than the 4-minute processing time, so messages reappear and a second worker takes them; raise the queue's visibility timeout above the longest processing time.

Make the consumer idempotent: record the order ID with a conditional write (for example in DynamoDB) before charging and skip IDs already seen; FIFO deduplication only covers a 5-minute window, so it cannot catch a resend hours later.
EventBridge rule on the default event bus matching EC2 Instance State-change Notification with state stopped; targets the Lambda function and an SNS topic with an email subscription.

Target tracking on backlog per instance: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible divided by the number of in-service instances, with the acceptable backlog per instance (latency goal / processing time per message) as the target.
Subscribe the returns queue directly to the SNS topic with a subscription filter policy on the order-type message attribute; remove the function.
Enable partial batch responses: ReportBatchItemFailures on the event source mapping and return batchItemFailures with the failed message IDs, so only those messages return to the queue.
Subscribing through the API does not edit the queue policy; add a queue policy statement allowing sns.amazonaws.com sqs:SendMessage with an aws:SourceArn condition equal to the topic ARN.

Cross-account access needs both sides: keep the role's identity policy and add a queue policy statement in account A that allows the role ARN sqs:SendMessage on that queue only. SSE-SQS needs no KMS permissions.

The AWS managed key's policy cannot be edited, so SNS cannot use it. Create a customer managed KMS key for the queue and add a key policy statement that lets the SNS service principal use kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt.
Poison messages: configure a dead-letter queue with a redrive policy (maxReceiveCount) on the source queue.
SNS-to-SQS fan-out: publish each order to an SNS topic, subscribe one SQS queue per service; each queue buffers its service's copy while it is offline.
Alarm on ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage of the queue.
